proof: A background command outlives a hard kill of the Core; the restarted Core reattaches to the same broker with no duplicate start, reads on from the acknowledged cursor without gap or repeat, replays the earlier output, refuses a reader with the old replay generation, and cancel ends the real process with a sealed OutputRef; the protocol state carries the handle and cursor across the restart. A hard-killed broker comes back with its sessions durable: a running one is LOST with exit unknown and a replayable sealed log, a retry replays it, an exited one keeps its exit code; an orphaned broker stops its process and exits.
audit: PARTIAL before: handles survived a client restart only; the broker died with the Core, sessions were in memory, attaches carried no generation, and nothing about handles or cursors was on the log.
limitations: A session lost with the broker is not restarted by the Core; browser and sandbox cursors are interfaces without producers until M7/M8; the orphan grace (60 s) bounds how long a dead Core's commands survive.
